text:
Alex W.: FYI — after enabling the continuous micro-batcher on prod (v2.3.1) this morning, we see ~12% drop in prefix-cache hit-rate for a few high-throughput tenants and median gen latency is +30ms. Dumping profiles now. :eyes:
Maria G.: ugh, any idea which model/variant + region?
Alex W.: mostly r-instruct-1.0 on us-west-2. Quick metric snippet: 
```
hit_rate_before: 0.78
hit_rate_after: 0.68
p50_latency_before: 82ms
p50_latency_after: 112ms
backlog_spike: +220 reqs/min around 09:12
```
Ryan K.: did the cache keying change land with that deploy? we had the "tight keyer" change in the PRs last week.
Alex W.: yep — keying change is probably the culprit. New keyer adds a session tag to the prefix key to prevent cross-session bleed. snippet: 
```
// new key derivation
cache_key = sha256(model + "|" + prefix_hash + "|" + session_tag)
```
Alex W.: that made previously-shared prefixes appear unique across sessions, so warm prefixes aren't matching across requests that used to join the KV cache.
Maria G.: can we confirm whether it’s the session_tag specifically or the hashing order? any perf traces?
Alex W.: attaching top flame for a cold vs warm request (pasted): 
```
cold_request: kernel_lookup(12ms) -> kv_lookup(18ms) -> comp_kernel(40ms)
warm_request: kv_lookup(6ms) -> comp_kernel(38ms)
```
Alex W.: after the roll, kv_lookup time variance increased and hit-rate fell. The increased misses cascade into bigger batches with bigger lifetimes -> more queueing.
perf-bot: deploy-log: continuous-batcher v2.3.1 rolled at 2276520000 by infra-deploy-bot. keyer change shipped in PR #4123.
sre-oncall: seeing queueing backlog spike in the slab group hosting the affected tenants: 
```
09:10:03 queue_size=5
09:11:50 queue_size=42
09:12:12 queue_size=68
09:13:00 dropped=0 (timeouts increased)
```
Ryan K.: two hypotheses: (1) keyer uniqueness caused cross-request dedupe loss -> hit-rate drop; (2) continuous-microbatcher altered batch composition so short-prefix requests are mixed with long ones, reducing prefix-warmup frequency (hot prefixes no longer get re-used inside a burst). Both can explain latency uptick.
Maria G.: agree. quick mitigation options: revert keyer change, or roll back micro-batcher, or temporarily bias batcher to co-locate similar prefix_hash groups (cohorting).
Alex W.: I can roll a canary: pin batcher to pre-v2.3.1 kernel on one slab, and also run a small revert of session_tag inclusion on a different canary. Will run A/B and compare hit_rate and p50.
Alex W.: proposed experiment commands: 
```
# pin slab A to old keyer
infractl pin --slab slab-a --image continuous-batcher:v2.3.0
# slab B keeps v2.3.1 but we patch key derivation
infractl patch-config --slab slab-b --set "keyer.include_session=false"
```
Maria G.: sounds good. also can we try increasing prefetch window/warmup budget for a short period to see if that recovers hit-rate? maybe tweak prefetch=0.6 -> 0.8.
Ryan K.: yes — batcher has tunables: cohort_window, max_prefetch, batch_ttl. my vote: cohort_window += 50ms and max_prefetch += 20%. that should bias microbatches to group same-prefix requests and increase warm reuse.
Alex W.: running the two-canary plan now. I'll post numbers in ~20m. Action items: Alex rolls canaries, Maria prepares rollback plan, Ryan prepares cohorting patch if needed.
Maria G.: thanks. ping me if rollback required, I'll coordinate customer comms. :pray:
perf-bot: perf-alert: observed regressed hit-rate across 3 tenants after 2276520000 (delta -0.10, p<0.01).
Alex W.: early canary results (10m in): slab-a (pinned pre-roll) hit_rate=0.77, slab-b (patched keyer) hit_rate=0.75, prod (v2.3.1) hit_rate=0.68. p50 follows similar pattern. Looks like session_tag inclusion is the main driver, cohorting helps but keying dominates.
Ryan K.: then we should revert session_tag inclusion and re-evaluate. Also ticket to add an opt-in flag gating key uniqueness per-tenant.
Alex W.: opening rollback PR and a postmortem ticket. Will also add a regression test exercising continuous-batcher + keyer combos in staging with synthetic prefix churn.
Maria G.: awesome—thanks. keep updates short here.
